question: Explain the relief from double taxation available under sections 90 and 91 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, including what a non-resident must furnish to claim treaty benefits.

points.label: Bilateral relief through agreements
points.description: The Central Government may enter into agreements with other countries or specified territories to grant relief from double taxation, avoid double taxation, exchange information and recover tax; such agreements must not create opportunities for non-taxation or reduced taxation through evasion or avoidance, including treaty shopping.

points.label: Treaty or Act, whichever is more beneficial
points.description: Where an agreement applies, the provisions of the Act apply only to the extent they are more beneficial to the assessee; however, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule applies even if it is not beneficial to the assessee.

points.label: Tax residency certificate and other information
points.description: A non-resident can claim treaty relief only on obtaining a tax residency certificate from the government of its country of residence, and must also furnish the other prescribed information (Form 10F); the certificate is necessary but not by itself sufficient.

points.label: Unilateral relief
points.description: Where there is no agreement, a resident who has paid tax in another country on income that accrued and was taxed there gets a deduction from Indian tax of the doubly taxed income at the lower of the Indian rate and the foreign rate.

points.label: Claiming foreign tax credit
points.description: A resident claims credit for foreign tax under an agreement or section 91 in the manner set out in the Income-tax Rules, and furnishes the prescribed statement of foreign income and tax (Form 67).
